Routing notes:
- Only confirmed success: REQ-2400, large refund from North, routed to C (regional office). This may depend on additional context; do not generalize.
- C was rejected for: small shipments (North/South), small refunds (North/South), large refund North in a different submission, small East claim. Thus C is not a default for regional requests.
- B was rejected for a large East claim; no option is confirmed valid for claims.
- Requester notes such as urgency, repeat attempts, and “regional office” mention did not reliably indicate the correct option.
- No reliable routing rule or option mapping has been established. Use all request attributes and seek stronger evidence before selecting; avoid repeatedly defaulting to C.

Routing notes:
- Confirmed successes: REQ-2400 (large North refund → C), REQ-2411 (small South refund → D), REQ-2413 (small South refund → A), and REQ-2417 (small South shipment → D). These are context-specific; identical request types have produced different outcomes.
- C was rejected for small North/South shipments, small North/South refunds, a different large North refund, and a small East claim. Do not default regional requests to C.
- Claims remain especially uncertain: B has been rejected for a large East claim; A and D were rejected for small North claims; A was also rejected for a small South claim. No claim option is confirmed.
- A was rejected for a small East invoice and a small South claim, but accepted for a small South refund.
- B was rejected for a large East invoice as well as a large East claim.
- D was accepted for a small South refund and small South shipment, but rejected for a small South refund in another submission and a small North claim.
- Requester notes (“regional office,” urgency, repeat attempts, scanned paperwork, and receipt confirmation) have not yielded a reliable rule. Similar notes and request attributes can map to different options.
- No dependable routing rule or complete option mapping is established. Evaluate region, request type, size, requester/organizational context, and note together; treat every option as uncertain and avoid repeatedly selecting C, A, or D without stronger evidence.

Routing notes:
- Confirmed successes: REQ-2411 (small South refund → D), REQ-2413 (small South refund → A), REQ-2417 (small South shipment → D), REQ-2423 (large South refund → B), and REQ-2426 (large North shipment → D). Outcomes remain context-specific.
- C is repeatedly invalid for large North refunds (REQ-2420), large North claims (REQ-2421), and prior small North/South shipments, refunds, and other requests. Do not default to C.
- D worked for a large North shipment after a bounced first attempt, but failed for another large North shipment, a small East shipment, and some South/North requests. Do not generalize from it.
- B worked for one large South refund, but failed for another large South refund, a small South claim, a small North shipment, a small North refund, and prior large East invoice/claim cases.
- Claims remain unresolved: B failed for large East and small South claims; A and D failed for small North claims; A also failed for a small South claim. No claim option is confirmed.
- A remains mixed: accepted for a small South refund, rejected for a small East invoice and South/North claims.
- Notes such as “same as last month,” urgency, repeat attempts, receipt confirmation, and requester organization have not produced a reliable rule. Similar attributes still map to different options.
- No dependable routing rule or complete option mapping exists. Evaluate region, type, size, requester context, and note jointly; treat all options as uncertain and avoid defaulting repeatedly to C, A, B, or D.

Routing notes:

- B worked for one large South refund and a small North claim, but failed for another large South refund, large South/small North claims, small North shipment/refund, and prior large East invoice/claim cases.
- A worked for a small South refund but failed for small East invoice, small North refund/shipment, and South/North claims.
- Claims remain unresolved overall: only small East → D and small North → B are confirmed; large South → B/D failed, and prior North/South/East claim attempts were inconsistent.

- No dependable routing rule or complete option mapping exists. Evaluate region, type, size, requester context, and note jointly; treat every option as uncertain and avoid repeated defaults.

- Recent failures: small South claim→D (REQ-2441); large South claim→C (REQ-2442); large East refund→C (REQ-2443); large North shipment→D (REQ-2445); small South invoice→D (REQ-2449).
- C is valid in observed large East invoice and large East claim cases, but invalid for large North refunds/claims, large East refund, and various prior North/South requests. Never default to C.
- D is context-dependent: valid for listed small South refund/shipment, large North shipment (REQ-2426), small East claim, and large East claim; invalid for another large North shipment, small South claim/invoice, small East shipment, small North refund, and large South claims.
- B is valid for large South refund, small North claim/invoice, and some prior cases; it failed for another large South refund, multiple claims, and other North/East requests.

Routing notes:
- No dependable global routing rule or complete option map. Evaluate region, type, size, requester context, and note jointly; do not default or repeat a choice solely because a similar case succeeded.
- New confirmed successes: REQ-2451 small South refund→A; REQ-2453 small North invoice→B; REQ-2454 small East invoice→B.
- New failures: REQ-2450 and REQ-2458 large South refund→B; REQ-2452 small South refund→A; REQ-2455 small East refund→B; REQ-2456 large East invoice→C; REQ-2457 small East shipment→A; REQ-2459 small South shipment→D.
- Repeated outcomes show strong case-level variation: small South refund has both A successes and an A failure; large South refund has B failures despite an earlier B success; large East invoice has C successes and a C failure. Similar request attributes are insufficient.
- C is valid in some large East invoice/claim cases, but invalid for large East refund, one large East invoice, large North refunds/claims, and various North/South requests. Never default to C.
- D is valid for some small South refund/shipment, large North shipment, small East claim, and large East claim; invalid for another small South shipment, small South claim/invoice, small East shipment, small North refund, and large South claims. Do not infer D from region/type alone.
- B is valid for large South refund once, small North claim/invoice, and small East invoice; it failed for two additional large South refunds, small East refund, multiple claims, and other North/East requests.
- A has limited support: confirmed for some small South refunds, but failed for another small South refund and small East shipment.
- Requester identity/role and notes (urgency, repeat attempts, receipt confirmation, paperwork, organization, office origin) still provide no reliable standalone rule. Claims and shipments remain especially context-dependent.
